The method addresses the limitations of traditional parallel raycasting algorithms that divide workload by separation planes in screen space or object space (sort-first or sort-last), which often lead to perceivable boundaries due to deferred shading from warped images being only an approximation to per-sample phong shading [S1].

The source explicitly states that traditional parallel raycasting algorithms using separation planes (screen or object space) 'often lead to a perceivable boundary' because 'deferred shading from warped images is only an approximation to a per-sample phong shading.' It further explains that the method in question addresses these limitations by using flexible schemes (like quality maps based on disocclusions) instead of fixed separation planes.
